body:
Builds on the propagation work in #341 with lower-level changes to the shared expandBucket kernel, which serves both eager fields and the resumable building search:

- 64 buckets selected with a mask instead of signed % 43; any count above the largest edge cost keeps one cost per bucket.
- Flat per-bucket queues (GradientBucket) in place of std::vector push_back: one reservation per expanded cell, appends without branching, and one shared cold grow path instead of eight inlined.
- Straight and diagonal entry costs precomputed once per field rather than dividing by 10 per cell.
- Branchless relaxation, with the six above/below neighbours relaxed by SSE2 where available. GLOB2_GRADIENT_SCALAR forces the portable path so tests can cover it on x86.
- The loop-invariant resource-type lookup is hoisted out of resource seeding.

Each cell's value is its unique cheapest cost to a seed, and a paused building search stops only between whole cost layers, so queue order does not affect any field. A new test checks the kernel against a verbatim copy of the previous one on maps up to 256x256, all swim classes, deferred seeds and cost caps, including column-edge widths.


Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01MAQdSLEK2hF2eJ3semGTxT
title: Speed up the gradient kernel without changing its results
